steps.label: Known PFAS-related health effects
steps.text:
• Developmental Problems in Children
• Increased Risk of Cancer
• Weakens Effectiveness of Immune System
• Interference with Natural Hormones
• Increased Cholesterol

steps.label: Why Not Just Remove Them?
steps.text: PFAS are often too small to filter away. They also contain Carbon-Fluorine bonds which are too strong to break, giving them the nickname 'Forever Chemicals'.

steps.label: Strong Bonds!
steps.text: Carbon-Flourine bonds are some of the strongest in organic chemistry, making them immune to damage from oil, water, or heat. By not breaking, these chemicals bioaccumulate, amplifying their harmfulness.

steps.label: But not all PFAS are the same
steps.text:
Ultra-short chain PFAS (with 2-3 carbon atoms) and short-chain PFAS (with 4-6 carbon atoms) easily dissolve in water, meaning they travel wherever water moves and are harder to filter.
Long-chain PFAS (at least 7 carbon atoms) do not dissolve so easily in water, but their length allows them to be absorbed by our body in higher concentrations.
